notes: Training rewards score the policy's generated conditions (policy-dependent). The held-out figure scores dataset records (policy-independent).

The loss/objective is preserved exactly (sequence-mean ratio, clip 0.2, value MSE 0.5, detached KL, sampled-token entropy 0.01). The recorded run divided the summed PPO-epoch losses by 4 before one optimizer step; the framework averages over PPO epochs (divides by 3). Adam is invariant to a constant gradient scale apart from epsilon and gradient-norm clipping, so the result is expected to transfer, but reproducing the exact numbers is recommended before using them as a regression target.
The run log notes the script raised an error after saving results; training and evaluation had completed.

Training rewards do not measure policy quality in this run. Records carry nested `outcomes`, which take precedence over any keys decoded from the generated JSON, and the rule reward reads only yield/selectivity/safety/steps, so each iteration's reward is the mean rule score of the 4 sampled training records (pinned by tests/unit/test_benchmark_semantics.py). Sampling 4 random records from records 0-399 reproduces the logged statistics: mean of logged iteration rewards 0.848 simulated vs 0.850 recorded, and a best-of-200 batch mean with median 0.9014 (P(>=0.9007) = 0.56) vs the recorded 0.9007. The held-out value equals the pure rule score of records 400-499, consistent with the reward model falling back to the rule (untrained learned reward model).
The JSON was assembled from the console log (values rounded to 4 decimals, logged every 10 iterations); iteration 0.9007 is not among the logged iterations.
The 100 held-out records are all Ketoprofen: the file is ordered by molecule (100 each) and the split takes the last 20%.
